warnings.description: Headline ratio rounds to 1e-5 in ab_results.json/.md (ratio_axiom_over_llama_tflops); the load-bearing/unambiguous number is llama_over_axiom_speedup_tflops=87289.22 and the prose '~87,000x'. Not a bias — the rounded ratio is only the inverse of the disclosed speedup — but a reader skimming only the rounded ratio gets a lossy value. Cosmetic; the speedup field and prose are exact.

fairness_caveat says '~structurally 100x under-parallelized' while the headline is ~87,000x. This is NOT a contradiction (100x ~ 1-of-188-SM parallelism deficit is ONE of the two stacked deficits; the other is 1/4096 work + latency-bound single workgroup), and DESIGN/BENCHMARKS decompose it correctly. But the bare '100x' in the JSON caveat, read in isolation, could be misread as understating the gap. The decomposition prose elsewhere is correct and present.

SPIRV-Headers build workaround is recorded in DESIGN §3.1.19 (reproducibility) and in the script header/comments, but the SPIRV_HEADERS_PREFIX install step itself is operator-provided (not scripted). A naive re-runner on the same box must know to `cmake --install` SPIRV-Headers into vendor/spirv-headers/install. The workaround is documented, so reproducibility is preserved, but it is a manual prerequisite, not automated.

fairness_checks.flop_parity_each_side_own_M: PASS — AXIOM flops = 2*K_CONTRACTION = 2*1*14336 = 28672 (M=1, bench line 317; JSON flops_per_dispatch=28672). llama recompute = 2*llama_m*n_eff*llama_k = 2*4096*1*14336 (emitter line 72). Each side's TFLOPS uses ITS OWN M. No accidental M=4096 on the AXIOM side (that would be 4096x flatter). Verified arithmetic: 28672/315456e-9/1e12=9.1e-5 (min), /338668e-9=8.5e-5 (sustained), ratio 8.5e-5/7.39=1.15e-5 => 87289x. All consistent.

summary: APPROVE. This is an honest, fairness-controlled benchmark A/B with no measurement bias in EITHER direction. (1) The headline ratio is matched-boundary: AXIOM sustained-CPU-wall vs llama.cpp sustained-CPU-wall MEAN (emitter line 95); GpuTimestamp MIN is disclosure-only and is NOT the kill number — and AXIOM's WORSE (sustained) number is the one used, so AXIOM is never flattered. (2) FLOP parity is correct: each side's TFLOPS uses ITS OWN M (AXIOM 2*1*14336=28672; llama 2*4096*1*14336); no accidental 4096x inflation — I re-derived the arithmetic and it matches. (3) The selected llama.cpp op is genuinely n==1 (GEMV); GEMM substitution is forbidden and the absent-case path is a real fail-closed INCOMPLETE. (4) Reproducible: literal 40-char SHA pinned + runtime-verified, full provenance in ab_results.json, vendor/ gitignored (0 tracked), build workaround documented (one manual prereq, noted as a warning). (5) Honest framing in both directions: the 1-row-vs-4096-row caveat is present everywhere, kill_criterion is mechanically FAIL, the NVIDIA-only != project-kill qualifier is present, the 1/4096-work + dispatch-latency decomposition is correct, and the FAIR throughput metric was chosen (a raw-us comparison would have FLATTERED AXIOM). (6) AT-1761 bit-exactness gates both the bench pre-flight and a GPU integration test. (7) No regression: zero compiler-src changes, additive only, no unwrap-panic in new code. Three non-blocking warnings: the rounded 1e-5 ratio is lossy (the exact 87,289x speedup field carries the real number), the bare '~100x' in the JSON caveat could be misread in isolation (the full decomposition is correct and present elsewhere), and the SPIRV-Headers install is a manual prerequisite (documented but not scripted). None of these affect fairness, the verdict, or reproducibility of the numbers. Most dangerous residual: the SPIRV-Headers manual prereq is the only non-automated step in an otherwise one-command reproduction — a re-runner on a clean box could be blocked at build until they install it, but it is documented and fail-closed (FATAL if test-backend-ops does not build, never a fabricated number).
